title: Enhancing mathematics education for students with special educational needs through generative AI: A case study in Greece
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether generative AI, specifically ChatGPT 3.5, can be used to create individualized mathematics lesson plans and worksheets for students with special educational needs in a general K-12 classroom. The authors frame the study around a gap in prior research on AI-supported worksheet and lesson-plan creation for inclusive mathematics instruction, and they introduce a new concept, “mathematical familiarity,” to describe how well AI-generated materials align with students’ interests and needs.

The study reports a nine-hour teaching intervention in a Greek middle school classroom with two 8th grade students: one diagnosed with dyslexia and the other with autism spectrum disorder. Using prompts in ChatGPT, the researchers generated customized worksheets for topics including square roots and irrational numbers, then observed how the students responded to the materials during regular classroom lessons. Data came from interviews, tasks, an e-questionnaire, and classroom observation, and were analyzed qualitatively with contingency/content analysis and a triangulation approach.

The paper concludes that the AI-generated worksheets appeared to increase engagement, comfort, and confidence, and that the students performed well on class tasks and tests during the intervention. The authors argue that ChatGPT can help teachers rapidly produce differentiated materials that reflect learners’ interests and special educational needs, though they also emphasize that teachers still need to use judgment when prompting and reviewing outputs. The study is presented as an exploratory case study rather than a causal comparison, and it is most directly evidence about lesson-plan/worksheet generation in K-12 special education contexts, not instructional coaching or lesson-plan feedback.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed qualitative case study with multiple data sources, but it is not causal and has only two participants. It provides descriptive evidence and triangulated observations, but credibility and generalizability are limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports promising positive outcomes for a very small, priority population sample, but no effect sizes and no controlled comparison are provided. The impact is therefore plausible but unclear and modest in evidentiary strength.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT 3.5 used to generate individualized mathematics lesson plans and differentiated worksheets for two 8th-grade students with special educational needs (dyslexia and ASD) in a general classroom, tailored to their curriculum, interests, and hobbies.

finding.finding_summary: This qualitative case study reports that two 8th-grade students with special educational needs (n=2) were able to understand the square root of a positive number and irrational numbers more satisfactorily when taught with ChatGPT-generated differentiated worksheets. Their performance on class tests was described as correct or almost correct, but no statistical effect size was reported.
finding.measure: Teacher-administered mathematics exercises and tests on square roots and irrational numbers; interview responses about understanding

finding.finding_summary: The students reported feeling safe, confident, comfortable, and enthusiastic when the worksheets reflected their interests and everyday lives. The paper argues that the ChatGPT-generated worksheets increased engagement and positive attitudes toward mathematics, based on interview and questionnaire responses from n=2 students and the classroom teacher’s observations.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interviews, e-questionnaire ratings, teacher observations of engagement and confidence

finding.finding_summary: The paper qualitatively suggests that the intervention supported problem solving and active participation, as students connected mathematical tasks to real-life contexts and completed exercises independently. However, this is based on descriptive evidence from a two-student case study rather than a controlled measure of durable skills.
finding.measure: Interview responses and observed task completion; indirect references to problem solving and participation

finding.finding_summary: The authors claim ChatGPT allowed the teacher to prepare individualized worksheets and lesson plans in a relatively short time, suggesting reduced preparation burden. This outcome is asserted descriptively rather than measured with time-on-task or workload metrics.
finding.measure: Author-reported teacher preparation process and practical suggestions
